item_arguments_and_dependencies.claim_and_conventions: For a Borel probability on a separable real Banach space, the support defined by positive mass on every norm-open neighborhood is Borel and has full measure.

source_locators.locator: §4.1, Theorem 4.3 and proof motivate the support-point route; the countable-base/full-measure lemma is proved locally to repair the bounded-noncompact-set shortcut.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.claim_and_conventions: On a closed bounded data ball, weighted lower-envelope and data-Lipschitz assumptions imply uniform positive evidence and a linear library root-L2 Hellinger stability bound; the optional TV branch separately assumes AC.

source_locators.locator: §4.1, Theorems 4.3 and 4.5 and their proofs (PDF pp. 36–39). The local uniform lower evidence bound is proved by a support-point neighborhood; the printed bounded-noncompact-set supremum shortcut is not used. This source uses a 1/sqrt(2) Hellinger normalization; the item uses root-L2 and recomputes constants.

§3.1, Example 3.1; §3.4, Assumptions 3.5, Theorem 3.6 and Lemma 3.7 with full proof (PDF pp. 7–12 and 24–25). The source proves Hellinger continuity under dominated-likelihood hypotheses, not the stronger IP-17 Lipschitz modulus; it also uses a 1/sqrt(2) Hellinger normalization, so constants are recomputed locally.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.claim_and_conventions: A shared weighted integrable lower envelope and pointwise potential error M2(||u||)psi_N imply eventual O(psi_N) root-L2 Hellinger error between the fixed-data updates.

source_locators.locator: §4.2, Theorems 4.8 and 4.9 and their proofs (PDF pp. 40–43). The local positivity proof is replaced by IP-16 propriety plus a normalizer perturbation bound; the printed bounded-noncompact-set supremum shortcut is not used. This source uses a 1/sqrt(2) Hellinger normalization; the item uses root-L2 and recomputes constants.

§2, Theorems 2.4 and 2.6 with complete proofs (PDF pp. 7–10), and Appendix A, Definition A.2 (PDF pp. 33–34). The paper's Hellinger distance includes a factor 1/sqrt(2); the library root-L2 convention is used here, and the local constant is recomputed.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.claim_and_conventions: An equal two-point prior with Phi(u;y)=(y-u)^2/2 has explicit evidence and logistic posterior mass and satisfies the weighted stability hypotheses on every bounded datum interval.

source_locators.locator: §4.1, Theorem 4.5 and proof: weighted integrability gives Hellinger Lipschitz stability.
§3.4, Lemma 3.7 and proof: likelihood continuity gives Hellinger continuity under an integrable dominator.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.claim_and_conventions: The prior c/n^2, base potential 0, and approximants n/N have positive finite evidence but Hellinger error bounded below by a constant times N^-1/2, disproving a universal O(N^-1) rate without weighted integrability.

source_locators.locator: §4.2, Theorem 4.9 and proof (PDF pp. 40–43); its linear rate requires weighted integrability.
§2, Theorems 2.4 and 2.6 with proofs (PDF pp. 7–10): a linear rate uses an integrable envelope, while a separate compact/tail argument yields convergence without that rate.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.claim_and_conventions: A three-point prior and explicit positive potentials give symmetric posterior laws with equal zero means but library root-L2 Hellinger distance greater than one.

source_locators.locator: §4.1, Remark 4.6: Hellinger control yields expectation control only with second-moment hypotheses.
Appendix A, Lemma A.3: the Hellinger-to-moment direction has explicit moment hypotheses.
